description: A student is planning a 4-year path from a Bachelor's in Singapore to a PhD in the US. They need to track research projects, faculty relationships, and publication goals over several years to ensure they are competitive for top-tier graduate schools.

user_profile.context: Starting their first year, wants to build a portfolio that 'future-proofs' their PhD application
user_profile.communication_style: Visionary, likes to connect current actions to 5-year goals

fact_sheet.fact: Alex Tan is a first-year undergraduate student pursuing a Bachelor of Science in Computational Neuroscience at Meridian University of Singapore (MUS).
To be eligible for the NeuroAI Lab, Alex must complete CS2109: Introduction to AI with a grade of A- or better by the end of Year 1, Semester 2.
Alex's target cumulative GPA to remain competitive for top-5 US PhD programs is 4.8 out of 5.0.
Alex has planned to take BN3301: Advanced Neural Data Analysis in Year 3, Semester 1, taught by Dr. Kenji Tanaka.
Alex Tan's assigned freshman academic advisor is Dr. Priya Sharma, whose office is located at MUS Science Tower 2, Room 04-112.
In his second semester, Alex plans to join Project 'CerebroSim,' which focuses on simulating cortical column activity using Python and the Brian 2 simulator.
Project 'CerebroSim' is supervised by Dr. Lena Petrova in the NeuroAI Lab at MUS.
Alex's primary goal for his first six months on Project 'CerebroSim' is to complete a literature review of 50 key papers on neural simulation, managed in a shared Zotero library.
For his third year, Alex is targeting a position on Project 'CogniPath' with Dr. Kenji Tanaka, which investigates reinforcement learning models of human decision-making.
The Git repository for Project 'CerebroSim' is hosted on the lab's private GitLab server at git.neuroai.mus.edu.sg/cerebrosim.
The NeuroAI Lab is located in the MUS Institute for Neurotechnology, Wing B, Level 3, with Alex's assigned workstation being B3-S12.
Alex plans to email Dr. Evelyn Reed at Stanford University in August 2026 to inquire about potential research opportunities and a campus visit.
The NeuroAI Lab holds its weekly progress meetings every Friday from 3:00 PM to 4:30 PM SGT in meeting room IN-03-MR5.
Alex aims to attend the CogSci 2025 conference in Sydney, Australia to present a poster on his initial findings from Project 'CerebroSim'.
In his first meeting with Dr. Petrova, Alex will ask, 'What are the key unsolved challenges in simulating synaptic plasticity that this lab aims to address in the next 3 years?'
The target venue for Alex's first co-authored paper from Project 'CerebroSim' is the main track of the NeurIPS 2026 conference.
The internal deadline to submit a full draft of the NeurIPS 2026 paper to Dr. Petrova for review is March 15, 2026.
Alex's aspirational goal for his final year project is a first-author publication in the 'Journal of Computational Neuroscience'.
Alex has scheduled to take the GRE General Test on June 30, 2026, to ensure scores are available well before application deadlines.
Alex's list of potential recommenders for his PhD applications includes Dr. Lena Petrova, Dr. Kenji Tanaka, and his future Final Year Project supervisor.
The application deadline for the Carnegie Mellon University (CMU) Neuroscience PhD program is December 1, 2026, at 11:59 PM EST.
Alex tracks all PhD application components, deadlines, and faculty contacts on a Notion page located at the private URL notion.so/alextan/phd-app-tracker-2027.
Stanford University's Computer Science department requires a minimum TOEFL iBT score of 100 for PhD applicants.
Alex plans to apply for the A*STAR National Science Scholarship (NSS) in his second year, which funds PhD studies abroad for Singaporean citizens.
The estimated application fee for the PhD program at Stanford University is $125 USD, which Alex has budgeted for in his application plan.
